questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(5,9,-6)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $3x+2y+7z=-9.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=2$ and $y=3$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+2y+7z & =-9 \\ 3(2)+2(3)+7z & =-9 \\ 7z & =-21 \\ z & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(2,3,-3)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,3,-3⟩-⟨5,9,-6⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-6,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨3,2,7⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-3)\cdot 3+(-6)\cdot 2+3\cdot 7|}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{7}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-9-12+21|}{\sqrt{9+4+49}} \\  & =\frac{|\,0\,|}{\sqrt{62}} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $P$ lies on the plane.

questions.problem: Given that $Q(4,0,-3)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨1,-4,5⟩=-11$, find the shortest distance from $P(-2,1,-1)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨4,0,-3⟩-⟨-2,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨6,-1,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨1,-4,5⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|6\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-4)+(-2)\cdot 5|}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{5}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|6+4-10|}{\sqrt{1+16+25}} \\  & =\frac{|\,0\,|}{\sqrt{42}} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $P$ lies on the plane $Π.$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,3,4⟩-⟨5,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-4,2,0⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-4)\cdot (-4)+5\cdot 2+1\cdot 0|}{\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|16+10+0|}{\sqrt{16+4+0}} \\  & =\frac{|26|}{\sqrt{20}} \\  & =\frac{13\sqrt{5}}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-7,5,2)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $4x-8y+8z=-36.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-1$ and $y=1$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-8y+8z & =-36 \\ 4(-1)-8(1)+8z & =-36 \\ 8z & =-24 \\ z & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-1,1,-3)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-1,1,-3⟩-⟨-7,5,2⟩ \\  & =⟨6,-4,-5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨4,-8,8⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|6\cdot 4+(-4)\cdot (-8)+(-5)\cdot 8|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-8)^{2}+{8}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|24+32-40|}{\sqrt{16+64+64}} \\  & =\frac{|\,16\,|}{\sqrt{144}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-2,5,-3)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $4x-4y+2z=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=1$ and $y=1$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-4y+2z & =2 \\ 4(1)-4(1)+2z & =2 \\ 2z & =2 \\ z & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(1,1,1)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,1,1⟩-⟨-2,5,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-4,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨4,-4,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|3\cdot 4+(-4)\cdot (-4)+4\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|12+16+8|}{\sqrt{16+16+4}} \\  & =\frac{|36|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{36}{6} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
